historical_claims.anchor: The novel was published in 1939, during the Great Depression, and draws on mass displacement from the southern Plains and surrounding states toward California.

The National Archives documents the combined role of drought, banking and agricultural transformations, oversupplied labor markets, and the federal migrant camps that tried to improve living conditions.
National Archives research explicitly documents that longer labor history.
She gathered material from migrant labor camps and worked on her own novel about displaced families, Whose Names Are Unknown.
Steinbeck did extensive field research and developed a relationship with Tom Collins, a federal migrant camp manager whose reports and experiences helped shape the book.

description: Analyzes Steinbeck’s The Grapes of Wrath through Depression-era migration, wage-setting power, intercalary chapters, Ma Joad’s leadership, Casy’s religious and political transformation, and solidarity beyond kinship. Considers the longer history of California’s diverse farm workforce and the contributions of Tom Collins and Sanora Babb to migrant testimony.
